authority_basis: Q-3 requires the true L0 of each acquired checkpoint to be measured empirically, because the published README's table and prose disagree about the direction of l1_weight -> sparsity and neither is trusted

readme_table.location: transcoder-adapters README lines 11-17, at the registered commit
readme_table.implied_direction: higher l1_weight -> HIGHER L0, meaning LESS sparse

readme_prose.location: transcoder-adapters README line 48, at the registered commit
readme_prose.claim: transcoder.l1_weight: L1 sparsity penalty - higher values produce sparser adapters with fewer active features per token
readme_prose.implied_direction: higher l1_weight -> LOWER L0, meaning MORE sparse

the_disagreement_being_adjudicated.note: the table's direction is also the counterintuitive one: a larger L1 penalty would normally produce a sparser representation, which is what the prose says

measurement.identical_conditions_for_both: same 200 val rows, same max_seq_len 1024, same code, same masking, batch_size 1, bf16

verdict.summary: NEITHER the table's values nor its claimed separation is reproduced, and the DIRECTION question is genuinely split by which summary statistic is used. This is reported as a split result rather than resolved in favour of whichever statistic tells a cleaner story.

on_values.finding: neither checkpoint reproduces its published L0
on_values.conclusion: the two checkpoints are far closer together in measured sparsity than the table implies, under every statistic computed

on_direction.per_layer_majority: 21 of 28 layers show the PROSE direction: the higher l1_weight checkpoint has the LOWER L0
on_direction.whole_model_median: supports the TABLE direction, but marginally, 1.7277 -> 1.8528
on_direction.why_the_statistics_disagree: layers 26 and 27 carry L0 values an order of magnitude above every other layer (23.33/24.39 and 18.40/37.25). Layer 27 alone differs by roughly 19 features per token between the checkpoints, which is enough to reverse the sign of the whole-model mean on its own.
on_direction.conclusion: the aggregate mean is dominated by two anomalous final layers; excluding them reverses the direction. A single-number answer to 'table or prose' cannot be given honestly from this measurement.

substantive_consequence_for_the_study.finding: the sparsity-sensitivity arm may have materially less leverage than its registered purpose assumes
substantive_consequence_for_the_study.reasoning: the sparsity sensitivity checkpoint is registered in authority 4.1 precisely to vary sparsity. If the two checkpoints differ by a factor of about 1.1 in measured L0 rather than the roughly 3.07 the table implies, then a sensitivity analysis contrasting them is contrasting two nearly equally sparse models on this data.
substantive_consequence_for_the_study.why_not: no L0 threshold is registered anywhere in the authority. Introducing one now, in either direction, would be inventing a criterion after seeing the measurement.
substantive_consequence_for_the_study.action_taken: recorded and reported to the operator; no threshold invented, no arm dropped, no registered decision altered

measurement_scope_caveat.statement: the absolute values here need not match the authors' published 'Val L0' figures, because the evaluation slice is almost certainly different: this measurement uses the first 200 usable rows of the registered OpenThoughts3-55k val split, truncated at 1024 tokens, taking problem and human-turn text only.
measurement_scope_caveat.what_this_caveat_does_not_undermine: the comparison BETWEEN the two checkpoints, which is apples to apples - identical rows, identical truncation, identical code, identical masking. The values are slice-dependent; the direction and the ratio are not.

claim_ceiling: This is an instrument measurement. It establishes what these two checkpoints do on this data slice. It is not evidence about J-space, about distillation, or about reasoning, and it is not a scientific result.
